title: A Study of Risvutatug Rezetecan in Combination With Atezolizumab in Participants With Extensive Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer (EMBOLD-SCLC-303)
summary: Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) is an aggressive type of lung cancer. Current treatment options are limited, and response to treatment may not last long. Outcomes are especially poor when the cancer has spread to the brain. This study tests whether a new treatment: risvutatug rezetecan (Ris-Rez) with atezolizumab works better than standard of care treatment. Ris-Rez is designed to deliver cancer-killing medicine directly to cancer cells. Atezolizumab helps the immune system attack cancer cells. Researchers will see if this combination helps people live longer and keeps the cancer from getting worse.

title: Global evolution of surgical complexity after neoadjuvant therapy: a bibliometric and quantitative trend analysis.
authors: Karataş O, Akyüz MS
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Integrating neoadjuvant therapy into the management of resectable non-small cell lung cancer has fundamentally altered operative decision-making worldwide, yet the evolution of surgical techniques (minimally invasive vs. open, anatomic vs. parenchyma-sparing) has not been fully mapped across global thoracic surgery centers. Although systemic therapy is used to downstage tumors and eradicate micrometastases, treatment-induced fibrosis and changes to the vascular architecture create intraoperative challenges that demand technical adaptation.
OBJECTIVES: In this study, we quantified 25 years of published articles on surgical responses to neoadjuvant therapy to identify geographic patterns of innovation and critical gaps in the reporting of functional outcomes.
METHODS: We performed comprehensive bibliometric mapping of 1,152 surgical oncology manuscripts (970 original investigations; 182 reviews) indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection from 2000 through 2024, analyzing institutional productivity patterns, international collaboration networks, and temporal shifts in research keywords related to the selection of operative techniques.
RESULTS: The volume of publications expanded at an annual rate of 11.69%. Chinese institutions generated 330 manuscripts-28.7% of the total number-emphasizing the development of minimally invasive techniques in the post-neoadjuvant therapy setting. Centers in the United States contributed 222 publications (19.3%), averaging 50.9 citations each. The United States centers were led by the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center (44 publications; 3,220 citations) and Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (30 publications; 3,357 citations), both of which pioneered parenchyma-preserving approaches. The immunotherapy era, from 2018 onward, showed a three-fold increase in the use of the keywords for "surgical complexity" and "postoperative complications," reflecting growing academic attention to technical challenges. Core thoracic journals included the Annals of Thoracic Surgery (28 articles) and Journal of Thoracic Oncology (32 articles).
CONCLUSION: Our analyses exposed critical imbalances between research focus areas and clinical priorities. Patient selection algorithms and respiratory function outcomes received disproportionately little attention, despite being fundamental to surgical decision-making. Only 12% of studies incorporated pulmonary function assessment, highlighting a research gap that requires immediate prioritization in the era of neoadjuvant therapy.

title: OR2B6 as a Prognostic Biomarker and Candidate Immunotherapeutic Target in Lung Adenocarcinoma: An Integrative Genomic and Transcriptomic Analysis.
authors: Ba Y, Liu Y, Lv H et al.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a common and aggressive subtype of non-small cell lung cancer, with a 5-year survival rate of less than 25%. Reliable biomarkers for prognosis and treatment remain urgently needed. This work explores the potential of OR2B6 as a prognostic biomarker and its relationship to immune infiltration in LUAD.
METHODS: RNAseq data of 539 LUAD and 59 normal tissues were obtained from TCGA. Differential expression, diagnostic value, prognosis, regulatory networks, immune infiltration, TMB, MSI, and drug sensitivity correlations of OR2B6 were analysed using various R packages and bioinformatics tools. Single-cell RNA-seq analysis was performed using TISCH2. Somatic mutation profiles of OR2B6 expression were examined. qRT-PCR was used to confirm OR2B6 expression in LUAD tissues and cell lines.
RESULTS: OR2B6 expression was significantly elevated in LUAD tissues compared to normal tissue (p < 0.001), with an AUC of 0.829 (95% CI: 0.792-0.866) for distinguishing LUAD from normal tissue. Elevated OR2B6 levels were linked to poorer overall survival (HR: 1.34; 95% CI: 1.00-1.79, p = 0.047) and disease-specific survival (HR: 1.55; 95% CI: 1.08-2.24, p = 0.019). OR2B6 remained independently associated with OS in multivariate Cox regression (HR = 1.376, p = 0.033). GSEA identified 9 pathways related to OR2B6, including immune-related pathways. OR2B6 expression showed a negative correlation with immune infiltration scores and HAVCR2, a positive correlation with LAG3, and positive correlations with TMB and MSI (p < 0.001). Somatic mutations associated with OR2B6 were identified, with a mutation rate of 0.39%. In silico analysis suggested that OR2B6 expression was associated with sensitivity to drugs including PLX4720 and Selumetinib; these findings require experimental validation.
DISCUSSION: OR2B6 is suggested to be a prognostic marker for LUAD. The observed association with immune infiltrations and immune checkpoint genes suggests that tumor immune evasion could be involved. The correlation with TMB and MSI further supports a potential role in immune response modulation. These findings provide a foundational basis for future research on OR2B6's role in LUAD and its potential as a candidate therapeutic target. As this is an exploratory analysis of public data, no a priori power calculation was performed, and the findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating pending validation in independent, adequately powered cohorts. Limitations include the use of public data and the need for functional validation.
CONCLUSION: OR2B6 represents a promising prognostic biomarker and candidate immunotherapy target in LUAD, with a promising association with clinical outcomes, immune infiltration, and drug sensitivity. However, these findings are correlative, and further functional and mechanistic studies are required to validate its therapeutic potential.

title: The spatial immune geography of resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: ecosystem architecture of perioperative immunotherapy response and relapse.
authors: Qi S, Zhou X, Liu C et al.
abstract: Perioperative immune-checkpoint blockade has improved pathological and event-free outcomes in resectable non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but benefit remains heterogeneous and current biomarkers do not reliably distinguish tumor eradication from transient control or future relapse. This limitation partly reflects how tumors are measured: programed death ligand 1 expression, tumor mutational burden and bulk immune-cell abundance compress a spatially organized ecosystem into summary values. Here, we define the spatial immune geography of resectable NSCLC across four coupled scales: intratumor territories, cellular neighborhoods, regional immune structures-including tertiary lymphoid structures and tumor-draining lymph nodes-and longitudinal transitions from pretreatment biopsy to resection, molecular residual disease and recurrence. We critically synthesize human evidence linking T-cell access, antigen-presentation circuits, B-cell and tertiary-lymphoid organization, and stromal, myeloid and hypoxic niches to perioperative immunotherapy response. We further distinguish pretreatment predictors from treatment-induced pharmacodynamic changes and explain why pathological response and biological cure are related but non-equivalent endpoints. On this basis, we propose a testable spatial-immune-resilience framework comprising eradication-permissive, persistence-prone and escape-permissive ecosystems. We also evaluate how multiplex imaging, spatial transcriptomics, digital spatial profiling, anatomically registered single-cell analysis and computational pathology differ in biological reach and translational readiness. Finally, we outline an assay-to-decision validation pathway that integrates standardized multiregion tissue sampling, tumor-draining lymph nodes and circulating tumor DNA. Spatial profiling is unlikely to transform perioperative care through maximal molecular resolution alone; its clinical value will depend on reproducible, parsimonious measurements that improve decisions beyond stage, pathology and molecular residual disease.

title: Efficacy and adverse reaction risk factors of immunotherapy in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: a retrospective study.
authors: Gao Q, Jin L
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of programmed cell death 1 (PD-1) inhibitors and identify risk factors for immune-related adverse reactions (irAEs) in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on data from 224 advanced NSCLC patients treated at the First Affiliated Hospital of Kunming Medical University between January 2021 and December 2022. The patients were divided into two groups based on the presence of adverse reactions after treatment: the irAE group (n = 117) and the non-irAE group (n = 107). General clinical data and treatment-related indicators were compared between the two groups, and the clinical therapeutic effect and incidence of adverse events were statistically evaluated. Finally, the influencing factors of immune-related adverse reactions in the patients were analyzed, and a corresponding prediction model was established.
RESULTS: The median survival time of the 224 patients was 23.5 months, with 1-year and 3-year survival rates of 88.5% and 32.1%, respectively. A total of 117 patients (accounting for 53.3%) experienced treatment-related adverse reactions, including fatigue, nausea, rash, and pruritus. Univariate and multivariate analyses indicated that smoking history, number of treatment cycles, and concurrent targeted therapy (TKI) were independent risk factors for immunotherapy-related adverse reactions in advanced NSCLC patients. The area under the curve (AUC) of the prediction model constructed based on the above factors was 0.768.
CONCLUSION: Patients with advanced NSCLC receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have a high incidence of irAEs, which are associated with their baseline patient characteristics. Smoking history, number of treatment cycles, and concurrent targeted therapy were identified as independent contributors.

title: Qingjin Desheng Pian attenuates NSCLC progression by suppressing neutrophil extracellular trap formation: involvement of the HMGB1/TLR2/MyD88 axis.
authors: Qin B, Huang S, Ma C et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Despite advances in immune checkpoint inhibitor-based therapy, a substantial proportion of patients derive limited benefit. In the tumor microenvironment, neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) promote tumor progression and metastasis, representing a potential therapeutic target. Qingjin Desheng Pian (QJDS) is a standardized hospital preparation of traditional Chinese medicine that has been used clinically for primary and metastatic lung cancer. Although earlier studies have suggested antitumor effects of QJDS, its impact on NET formation and the underlying mechanisms in NSCLC remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether QJDS suppresses NET formation and to elucidate the molecular mechanisms.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 209 stage III-IV NSCLC patients who received QJDS plus chemotherapy or chemotherapy alone. NET enrichment was assessed by single-cell RNA sequencing and histopathology. Network pharmacology predicted potential targets. A syngeneic Lewis lung carcinoma model evaluated antitumor efficacy and intratumoral NET levels. In vitro, primary mouse neutrophils were stimulated with phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA) for NET induction, followed by QJDS intervention. Transcriptomic sequencing and weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified hub genes. Pharmacological rescue experiments using N4-acetylcytidine (N4A) were performed.
RESULTS: QJDS prolonged progression-free survival, improved quality of life, and attenuated systemic inflammation. NETs were markedly enriched in NSCLC tumor tissues compared with adjacent tissues. QJDS dose-dependently inhibited tumor growth and reduced intratumoral NET formation and serum MPO-DNA levels in vivo. In vitro, QJDS suppressed NET release and attenuated NET-mediated migration, invasion, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and proliferation of lung cancer cells. Mechanistically, high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) was identified as a key hub gene through transcriptomic and weighted gene co-expression network analyses. QJDS significantly downregulated HMGB1, toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2), and myeloid differentiation primary response 88 (MyD88) expression in neutrophils, effects partially reversed by N4A.
CONCLUSION: These findings indicate that QJDS attenuates NSCLC progression by suppressing NET formation through mechanisms involving the HMGB1/TLR2/MyD88 axis, supporting its adjuvant application in advanced lung cancer.

title: Association Between Geographic Access to Lung Cancer Screening and Early-Stage Diagnosis.
authors: Lian M, Struthers J, Liu Y
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung cancer screening (LCS) centers are unevenly distributed across the United States, with much lower access in rural than urban areas. It remains unknown whether geographic access to LCS centers is associated with early detection of lung cancer.
METHODS: We used Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results data to identify patients aged 55-80 years diagnosed with lung cancer during 2015-2019. Geographic access to LCS centers was measured using the two-step floating catchment area method and categorized into quartiles. Modified Poisson regression with county-level clustering was used to estimate prevalence ratios (PRs) for early-stage diagnosis.
RESULTS: Patients in counties with the least access to LCS were less likely to be diagnosed at an early stage than those in counties with the greatest access (PR=0.88, 95% CI 0.84-0.93; Ptrend<.001). The association varied by neighborhood socioeconomic status and census region, with significant associations observed only among patients living in less deprived counties and in the Western United States. County-level vehicle ownership did not significantly modify this association overall, but among Medicaid beneficiaries residing in metropolitan areas, local transportation resources significantly modified the association between geographic access and early-stage diagnosis.
CONCLUSIONS: Limited geographic access to LCS centers was associated with a lower likelihood of early-stage lung cancer diagnosis, with variation according to neighborhood socioeconomic context, census region, and local transportation resource among Medicaid beneficiaries.
IMPACT: Geographic access to LCS centers is necessary, but not sufficient, for equitable LCS, and the benefits of improving geographic access depend on the broader socioeconomic, regional, and transportation context.

title: A miRpair-Based Molecular Comparator for Lung Cancer Diagnosis.
authors: Song J, Liu R, Gu L et al.
abstract: Early and precise cancer diagnosis is crucial for effective treatment. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are promising diagnostic targets, but translating their complex, multi-dimensional expression signatures into clinical practice remains challenging. Here, we develop a concise molecular comparator using relative expression levels of specific miRNA pairs. The miRpair-based strategy demonstrates superior diagnostic performance compared to methods relying on the absolute quantification of single miRNAs. For non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) diagnosis, we identify hsa-miR-148a-3p/hsa-miR-30d-5p as the optimal diagnostic pair from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) data, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.975. The silicon-based model achieves 90.3% accuracy in 93 clinical serum samples using quantitative analysis. We subsequently translate the comparator into a DNA-based molecular workflow via asymmetric polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and polymerase-assisted hybridization subtraction (PAH-Sub). This process performs threshold-based comparison of dual-miRNA relative abundance directly at the molecular level. Integration with catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) amplification generates fluorescent diagnostic outputs. Validation with 40 clinical serum samples yielded 87.5% accuracy, demonstrating the feasibility of molecular-level implementation of the miRpair decision rule. This study represents a proof-of-concept evaluation for NSCLC diagnosis. Further validation in independent cohorts incorporating clinically relevant disease controls will be required to establish broader clinical specificity.

title: Interfacial Charge-Regulated DNA Nanonets Enable Polarity-Switching Photoelectrochemical Liquid Biopsy of Lung Adenocarcinoma Circu-lating Tumor Cells.
authors: Jiang Y, Wang N, You H et al.
abstract: Conventional clinical diagnostic of lung adenocarcinoma relies heavily on computed tomography imaging combined with tissue biopsyan invasive workflow that drastically limits patient compliance and impedes early screening and dynamic monitoring. Although circulating tumor cells (CTCs) enable minimally invasive disease tracking, their clinical detection is severely compromised by ultralow abundance and complex hematological interferences. Herein, we present a dye-induced signal-reversal photoelectrochemical (PEC) biosensor for sensitive and accurate CTC detection in raw whole blood. Specific CTC recognition triggers a Mg2+-dependent DNAzyme-cascaded amplification, yielding abundant single-stranded DNA that programmably assembles into an acriflavine-confined nanonet at the electrode interface. This engineered nano-biointerface alters charge-transfer kinetics, thus driving a distinct anodic-to-cathodic photocurrent transition to effectively eliminate background noise and improve signal reliability, enabling ultrasensitive CTC quantification across a broad linear range (10-105 cells·mL-1) and an ultralow detection limit (0.11 cell·mL-1), along with excellent selectivity, stability, and reproducibility. Notably, clinical validation of the proposed biosensor using whole blood samples from lung adenocarcinoma patients (n = 78) and healthy donors (n = 22) shows high diagnostic accuracy (area under the curve = 0.9129) and strong consistency with radiologic findings. This engineered PEC sensing platform offered a robust, minimally invasive liquid biopsy strategy for early lung adenocarcinoma screening, therapeutic response assessment, and longitudinal disease management in personalized medicine.

title: Efficacy and safety of PD-L1 versus PD-1 inhibitors as consolidation therapy following concurrent chemoradiotherapy for unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer: a real-world retrospective study.
authors: Liu X, Qin Y, Lin Y et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The PACIFIC trial established consolidation immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) following concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cCRT) as standard care for unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Both programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) and programmed death‑ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitors are used, but their comparative effectiveness and safety remain uncertain.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted to compare survival and treatment-related pneumonitis between PD-1 and PD-L1 inhibitors consolidation therapy in 181 patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC who received ICIs following cCRT (May 2019-May 2024). Primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), and secondary endpoint was overall survival (OS). Survival curves were generated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Exploratory subgroup analysis was used to compare the survival benefit of the two drugs in populations with different clinical characteristics. Cox proportional hazards regression models were employed to identify factors associated with survival outcomes. Competing risk model was used to assess the risk of treatment-related pneumonitis.
RESULTS: PD-L1 consolidation was associated with significantly improved PFS compared with PD-1 inhibitors (adjusted HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.37-0.88, P = 0.011; log-rank P = 0.016). However, no statistically significant difference in OS was observed between the two groups (adjusted HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.32-1.11, P = 0.101; log-rank P = 0.052). Exploratory subgroup analysis demonstrated that PD-L1 inhibitors were associated with a lower hazard of disease progression in patients with a smoking history. The cumulative incidence of grade ≥ 2 pneumonitis showed no statistically significant difference between the two groups (P = 0.795), whereas the incidence of grade ≥ 3 pneumonitis was higher in the PD-L1 group, although this difference did not reach statistical significance (P = 0.244).
CONCLUSION: For patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC receiving cCRT, consolidation therapy with PD-L1 inhibitors may be associated with prolonged PFS compared with PD-1 inhibitors. Exploratory subgroup analysis suggested a greater benefit in patients with a smoking history. Owing to the limitations of this retrospective analysis, large-scale, multicenter studies with biomarker stratification are needed to optimize immunotherapy strategies.

title: The Drp1 inhibitor DRP1i2 confers cardioprotection against doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity.
authors: Deng Y, Bass-Stringer S, Bond ST et al.
abstract: Anthracyclines such as doxorubicin are highly effective chemotherapeutic agents, but their clinical use is limited by dose-dependent cardiotoxicity associated with mitochondrial dysfunction. Dysregulated mitochondrial dynamics, particularly excessive dynamin-related protein 1 (Drp1)-mediated fission, has been implicated in cardiac injury. We investigated whether DRP1i2, a novel small-molecule Drp1 inhibitor targeting a conserved domain, mitigates doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity while preserving anticancer efficacy. Cardioprotective effects were assessed in a murine model of chronic doxorubicin cardiotoxicity and in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiac microtissues, while anticancer activity was evaluated across multiple cancer cell lines in 2D and 3D systems. DRP1i2 preserved left ventricular systolic function in vivo, reduced interstitial fibrosis and cardiomyocyte atrophy, and attenuated myocardial proteomic remodelling. In human cardiac microtissues, DRP1i2 improved viability and restored contractile function despite persistent mitochondrial oxidative stress and metabolic dysfunction. In cancer models, DRP1i2 did not compromise doxorubicin efficacy across A549 lung cancer, OVCAR3 ovarian cancer, and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cell lines, and exhibited modest anticancer activity in MG63 osteosarcoma cells. These findings demonstrate that DRP1i2 confers cardioprotection while maintaining anticancer efficacy via modulation of Drp1-dependent mitochondrial dynamics, supporting mitochondrial fission as a targetable pathway to mitigate doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity.

title: DDR1: a potential pan-cancer prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in ECM remodeling and CAF infiltration.
authors: Jin D, Li J, Yang Z et al.
abstract: Discoidin domain receptor 1 (DDR1) is implicated in tumor progression, yet its clinical and molecular roles across cancers remain incompletely understood. To address this gap, we conducted a systematic pan-cancer analysis of DDR1 using multiple online databases, including The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), Tumor Immune Estimation Resource 2.0 (TIMER2.0), and cBioPortal for Cancer Genomics, and evaluated its expression, prognostic value, genomic alterations, tumor microenvironment associations, and functional networks. DDR1 was upregulated in 18 cancer types. In survival analyses, high DDR1 expression was significantly associated with favorable overall survival (OS) in kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (KIRC) and mesothelioma (MESO), and with unfavorable disease-free survival (DFS) in cholangiocarcinoma (CHOL), kidney chromophobe (KICH), and KIRC. High DDR1 expression was also associated with advanced pathological stage in several cancer types. Genomic amplification was the predominant alteration. DDR1 expression showed positive correlations with estimated cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) infiltration in multiple cancer types, although the strength and significance varied by deconvolution algorithm and cancer type. Functional analyses linked DDR1 to extracellular matrix (ECM) regulation and cell migration and proliferation. Notably, no significant correlation was observed between DDR1 and DDR2 expression across cancer types (R = -0.011, P = 0.26). Whether these two family members have divergent functions warrants further investigation. Collectively, these findings suggest that DDR1 may serve as a potential pan-cancer biomarker and candidate therapeutic target; however, further experimental and clinical validation is required.

title: Refractory Thymoma-Associated Minimal Change Disease Progressing to End-Stage Renal Disease: A Case Report.
authors: Ilyas M, Adi M, Ashraf A
abstract: Thymoma-associated minimal change disease (MCD) is an uncommon paraneoplastic cause of nephrotic syndrome in adults. Most reported cases respond to tumor-directed therapy and immunosuppression, but a small subset may be treatment-refractory and progress to renal failure. We report a 52-year-old man with prior resection and adjuvant radiotherapy for Type B2 (Masaoka stage III) thymoma who presented three years after cancer therapy with rapid weight gain, extensive peripheral edema, and frothy urine. Laboratory evaluation revealed nephrotic syndrome with 24-hour proteinuria 12.5 g, serum albumin 1.8 g/dL, and creatinine 1.4 mg/dL. Renal biopsy showed normal glomeruli on light microscopy, negative immunofluorescence, and diffuse podocyte foot-process effacement on electron microscopy, consistent with MCD. Prednisone 1 mg/kg/day failed to produce remission after four weeks. Staging with CT-PET identified an anterior mediastinal node consistent with recurrent thymoma, which was treated with targeted radiotherapy. Despite sequential immunomodulatory therapies-oral cyclophosphamide (months 2-8), tacrolimus (months 8-14), and two doses of rituximab (months 14-15)-proteinuria fluctuated but persisted at nephrotic levels and renal function progressively declined, with creatinine rising to 7.0 mg/dL by month 18, necessitating initiation of renal replacement therapy. The patient developed uremic symptoms and by month 18 required initiation of hemodialysis, ultimately transitioning to chronic peritoneal dialysis. This case documents an unusually aggressive course of thymoma-associated MCD refractory to multiple lines of immunosuppression and tumor-directed therapy, culminating in end-stage renal disease. It underscores that, although thymoma-related MCD is often steroid-responsive, clinicians should recognize the potential for refractory disease and consider early multidisciplinary management, vigilant oncologic surveillance, and exploration of alternative or targeted immunologic strategies in such patients.

title: Ocular Myasthenia Gravis Unmasking Molecularly High-Risk but Clinically Indolent Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia: A Case Report.
authors: Bin Khalid H, Furqan M, Ul Abedin Z et al.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: We report a patient who presented with acute-onset diplopia and fatigable ptosis, subsequently diagnosed with Myasthenia Gravis based on elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies. Neuroimaging and chest imaging were unremarkable, excluding structural causes and thymoma.
CASE PRESENTATION: During evaluation, persistent lymphocytosis prompted further hematologic workup, which confirmed early-stage Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia with trisomy 12 and a TP53 mutation. The patient received pyridostigmine and a tapering course of corticosteroids, resulting in rapid clinical improvement and complete resolution of ocular symptoms. The leukemia remained asymptomatic and was managed conservatively with a watchful waiting approach. The clinical course was favorable with sustained remission of myasthenia gravis off therapy and stable hematologic parameters on follow-up.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights the diagnostic interplay between autoimmune and lymphoproliferative disorders and underscores the importance of a multidisciplinary approach in managing such overlapping clinical entities.

title: Pleural Metastasis in Epithelioid Angiosarcoma.
authors: Alfonso Gamba MM, Barragan D, Gomez L et al.
abstract: Epithelioid angiosarcoma (EAS) is a rare, highly aggressive endothelial cell malignancy characterized by a propensity for rapid metastatic spread and an exceptionally poor prognosis. Diagnosing EAS remains a major clinical and histopathological challenge due to its atypical cellular morphology, mimicry of poorly differentiated carcinomas or mesotheliomas, and insidious, nonspecific clinical presentation, which frequently leads to diagnostic delays. Given the scarcity of literature on this entity, expanding the current clinical knowledge base is essential to facilitate early identification. In this report, we present the case of a 60-year-old woman with a history of pituitary adenoma resection who presented with progressive chest pain, weight loss, and symptomatic anemia, which initially suggested a non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), given the presentation of precordial pain and the results of the cardiac biomarker evaluation, but was later identified as metastatic disease. Imaging and biopsy revealed a rare metastatic EAS involving the liver, spleen, and pleura, prompting palliative care, video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS), and pleurodesis. This case serves as a critical reminder of the diagnostic challenges posed by atypical pleural metastases, which can uniquely mimic primary pulmonary or mesothelial malignancies. By highlighting this rare secondary manifestation, this report underscores the necessity of combining meticulous immunohistochemical analysis with a principal emphasis on thoracoscopic findings to confirm the diagnosis.

title: Controversies and consensus on immune function and long-term health risks following adult thymectomy: a comprehensive review of molecular mechanisms and real-world evidence.
authors: Zhao P, Li X, Wang X et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the long-term immunological, oncological, and clinical consequences of adult thymectomy by synthesizing recent basic, translational, and real-world clinical evidence.
BACKGROUND: Historical surgical paradigms regarded the post-pubertal adult thymus as an immunologically redundant, fatty involuted organ, justifying routine "incidental" resection during cardiac procedures. A high-profile 2023 cohort study in The New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM) challenged this concept, reporting that adult thymectomy significantly increased 5-year all-cause mortality and cancer risk. Subsequent population-level studies (US SEER/NCDB, French PMSI) and deep-learning imaging cohorts have sparked debate, offering both corroborating and conflicting insights into adult thymic function.
METHODS AND SYNTHESIS: This review synthesizes cellular mechanisms (TREC dynamics, TCR repertoire contraction, senescence-associated T cells, Treg lineage stability) and endocrine factors (thymulin-mediated myeloid regulation) with clinical data stratified by age at surgery, indication, resection extent, and follow-up duration.
CONCLUSIONS: The adult thymus remains functionally active, exporting naïve T cells and humoral immunomodulators like thymulin that maintain peripheral immune tolerance and restrain inflammaging. Clinical evaluation must differentiate between incidental resection (which induces avoidable iatrogenic immunosenescence) and therapeutic resection (e.g., for thymic epithelial tumors or myasthenia gravis), where removing a diseased, immunosuppressive microenvironment can reduce secondary cancer risk. Partial thymectomy (PT) is emerging as an option to preserve immunocompetence when oncologically feasible.

title: Access to systemic anti-cancer treatment in mesothelioma: a systematic review of inequities in treatment access and decision-making.
authors: Taylor B, Drury J, Montague-Hellen K et al.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To synthesise evidence on factors influencing access to and uptake of systemic anti-cancer treatment (SACT) for people with mesothelioma, an incurable cancer, with a focus on inequities in treatment pathways and decision-making within supportive oncology care.
METHODS: An integrative systematic review with narrative synthesis (PROSPERO: 603309) was conducted. APA PsycInfo, ASSIA, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, PubMed Central, Scopus and Web of Science were searched for English-language publications between 1 January 2008 and 18 October 2024. Eligible studies included empirical research and reproducible reviews reporting factors affecting access to or receipt of SACT among individuals with mesothelioma.
RESULTS: The search yielded 716 records, of which 18 met inclusion criteria. Four interrelated themes were identified: (1) demographic characteristics; (2) information provision and decision-making; (3) clinical and disease-related factors; and (4) healthcare system and structural factors. An overarching theme of intersectionality demonstrated how social, clinical and organisational influences interact to shape treatment access and decision-making.
CONCLUSION: Access to and uptake of SACT in mesothelioma is shaped by complex, interacting patient- and system-level factors, resulting in persistent inequities in treatment pathways. As SACT is typically delivered with palliative intent in this population, these findings highlight its role within supportive oncology care and the importance of equitable access, shared decision-making and consistent information provision across services.

title: Anterior Mediastinum.
authors: Rasmussen GR, Christophel E, Engelhardt KE
abstract: Anterior mediastinal tumors require deliberate, anatomy-driven operative planning within a confined space bordered by the innominate vein, superior vena cava, heart, and phrenic nerves. Although pathology informs overall management, operative success depends primarily on appropriate exposure and achievement of complete R0 resection. This article outlines diagnostic evaluation, staging principles, and surgical strategy. Open, minimally invasive, and combined approaches are discussed in the context of tumor size, invasion, and vascular involvement. Reconstruction, extracorporeal support, and complication management are reviewed, emphasizing that oncologic completeness, not incision choice, remains the central determinant of patient outcome.
